findings.reason: The definition allows arbitrary finite-dimensional real value spaces, but reverse mode and HVP use transposes and gradients without specifying inner products or a dual-cotangent convention. Specify Euclidean coordinate spaces and their standard products, or define cotangents and pullbacks in dual spaces.

Only operation cotangents are initialized to zero. Input cotangent accumulators are returned as the gradient but are never initialized, so their values are unspecified. Initialize all input cotangents to zero before seeding the output; define the seed if the output may itself be an input.

The binomial procedure promises a terminal value and starting cotangent, but its N=0 branch returns only the cotangent. T=0 is permitted by the capacity condition, so specify that this branch returns the known state x_a along with the unchanged cotangent.

The binomial correctness proof's N=0 base case does not account for the terminal value claimed in the theorem. State that the empty interval returns x_a and verify the returned value as well as the unchanged cotangent.

Proof step 2.1 imports the bound ||fl(B^T c)-B^T c|| <= gamma_n ||B||_F ||c|| without deriving it or citing a supplier fact. State gamma_n=nu/(1-nu), make the operationwise success assumptions explicit, and derive or cite the sequential real dot-product bound. The stated error formulas are sound under that bound.
